analysis.title: Market Rhythm Focus
key_insights: High yield spreads have widened beyond March levels, which the report calls historically a precursor to deeper equity selloffs. The move has hit market breadth, not the headline indices. Credit is flagging warning signals for SPX risk.

Semiconductors are extremely oversold short term, but the bigger trend looks damaged. The SOX/SPX ratio broke its 18-month uptrend, which historically leads to SPX weakness with a lag. Relative leadership is fading and risk is skewed lower.

The Transports ETF (IYT) bear flag has extended. It briefly closed above the 200-day moving average, then spent a full session back below it. A looming death cross reinforces the negative setup and downside risk.

The NYSE Composite shows fragile breadth, with only about 47% of stocks above their 200-day moving average. The index failed to hold the 50-day moving average after a short-lived reclaim, which reinforces a potential bear flag.

The S&P 500 was rejected from below at a trendline, with its lowest close in six weeks and a clear break of the recent range. Bias is lower, with downside risk toward the September intraday low around 7,508. The 200-day moving average is far below.

Tech has stabilized a bit, so the rest of the market is pausing. The S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF (RSP) remains above a falling 50-day moving average but is at risk of rolling over from a lower high, with fairly overbought conditions adding to that risk.

S&P 400 MidCap has not confirmed Equal Weight strength, which it usually accompanies. Mid Caps remain in a weak trend, with a falling 50-day moving average above and the index struggling to lift off the lows.

Euro Stoxx 50 printed a hammer candle under the 200-day moving average on Friday, hinting at reversal. Without a stronger bounce and a reclaim of the 200-day, 5,972 remains exposed. RSI is not oversold, so further downside is still possible.

sector_views.rationale: SOX/SPX ratio broke its 18-month uptrend, and relative leadership is fading, with risk skewed lower despite short-term oversold conditions.
IYT bear flag extended, with a close back below the 200-day moving average and a looming death cross.
S&P 400 MidCap is in a weak trend below a falling 50-day moving average and has not followed Equal Weight strength.

The SOX/SPX uptrend break historically leads to SPX weakness with a lag.

Weak breadth in the NYSE Composite and Mid Caps.
Euro Stoxx 50 could fall to 5,972 if it fails to reclaim the 200-day moving average.

NYSE Composite chart on page 5 shows the 50-day and 200-day moving averages and the percentage of stocks above the 200-day moving average, at about 47%.

RSP is described as fairly overbought, and Euro Stoxx 50 RSI is not oversold.
